offlineReplay512MiB.interpretation: The frozen predictor retains useful next-selection overlap across the five held-out prompts, with modest extra payload reads in fixed-route replay. This does not demonstrate that the speculative reads would improve live latency.

offlineReplay576MiB.interpretation: The current resident-refresh semantics degrade cache reuse on every held-out prompt. The predeclared preserve-resident variant avoids those effects and exactly matches demand-only cache counters in all five cases. With no new loads, it supplies no storage I/O to overlap at this budget.

limitations: This is five held-out prompts, one per category, not a broad statistical guarantee.
Only demand-only capture counters were measured on-device here. Candidate results are fixed-route offline replays assuming speculative reads complete before demand.
Neither a speedup nor an energy-saving effect has been measured for the cache-preserving variant. CPU overhead, scheduling, and asynchronous I/O timing are not simulated.
The current cache-refresh and proposed cache-preserving behaviors were both specified before the held-out capture; threshold 0.20 was not refitted.
The live Swift cache policy has not been modified by this offline analysis.
Payload byte counts do not directly measure physical NAND traffic.

decision.nextStep: Implement the cache-preserving resident-check behavior as a separately named experimental runtime policy, leaving existing ablations intact. Validate its integration with a small targeted device check only after tests and offline replay agree; do not repeat the held-out suite or power study merely to obtain more samples.
